title: Advanced Calculation Techniques
tagline: Year 4 — Algebraic identities, base-and-deviation, vedic-style methods and percentage fractions for fast exact arithmetic

introduction.overview: Fast exact arithmetic comes from a small toolkit: squaring numbers near a base, multiplying by 11, 25, 99 or 101, using (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b², and converting percentages to fractions. Each technique turns a long multiplication into two or three short steps. The tools are valid for every input; the skill is spotting when one applies.
introduction.placementRelevance: Calculation time decides how many questions you attempt; these techniques save 15–30 seconds on each arithmetic-heavy question.
introduction.realWorldContext: Mental arithmetic for bills, discounts and estimates uses the same shortcuts.

learningObjectives: Use a² − b² and (a ± b)² for products
Verify with digit sums (casting out nines)

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²; (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

coreDefinitions: Base: a convenient round number near the numbers being multiplied.
Deviation: the difference between a number and the base.
Digit sum: the repeated sum of digits, used to check products.
Complement: what a number lacks to reach a base.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Almost every awkward product is a nearby easy product plus a small correction.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Look for a base (10, 50, 100) or an identity. Compute the easy product, then add or subtract the correction.

mainNarrative: To find 53², write 50 + 3: 2,500 + 2 × 50 × 3 + 9 = 2,809. For 47 × 53 use the same centre 50: 50² − 3² = 2,491.
To multiply by 11, add adjacent digits: 346 × 11 = 3 | 3+4 | 4+6 | 6 = 3,806.
Percentage equivalents turn percentages into division: 12.5% of 640 = 640 ÷ 8 = 80; 16⅔% of 540 = 540 ÷ 6 = 90.

deepDiveAspects.title: Deviation method for 96 × 97
deepDiveAspects.content: Base 100: deviations −4 and −3. Cross-subtract 96 − 3 = 93 (or 97 − 4), then multiply deviations 12: 9,312.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why casting out nines works
deepDiveAspects.content: A number leaves the same remainder mod 9 as its digit sum; products preserve remainders.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Pick a base or identity, do the easy product, then correct.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Last digit of a product must match the product of last digits.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Memorise squares to 30 and fractions to 1/12.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: A shortcut that takes longer than direct multiplication is not a shortcut.
